item.description:
Portside can now work with files beyond this Mac — through its own SFTP panes
or as a real SMB network drive shared with Finder.

### What's new

- Connect to an SFTP server from Portside with a password or a Portside Key.
  New host keys are shown before trust, changed keys are refused, and saved
  remote tabs and Favorites return through an explicit Reconnect rather than a
  surprise network connection. Password storage is optional and scoped to the
  exact server endpoint in the macOS Keychain.
- Browse live remote folders, Quick View remote files, and transfer files
  between the Mac and SFTP with byte progress, cancellation, conflict choices,
  and recovery messages that name anything left behind. Local folders can be
  uploaded as complete trees; remote-source folder copies and decomposed folder
  merges fail closed instead of guessing at identity over SFTP. Writable SFTP
  panes support new folders and files, rename, copy and move within one live
  connection, and permanent removal of individual files and symbolic links.
- Mount an SMB network drive without leaving Portside. Mount Network Drive… is
  the first item in each pane's Volumes menu and in both Go-menu volume lists;
  macOS asks for credentials, the share appears in Finder too, and Portside
  opens the exact mounted volume in the pane that requested it.
- Keep Both joins Keep and Overwrite for name conflicts, choosing Finder-style
  copy names atomically so an existing item is never overwritten by the choice.
- Search now has Folder and Deep scopes. Folder is the familiar live filter;
  Deep walks local subfolders by name without following links or crossing the
  starting volume, stopping truthfully after the first 200 matches.
- Arrows move the commander cursor without changing marks; Space toggles the
  item under it and advances; Shift-arrow extends a marked range. File
  operations use the marks, or the cursor when nothing is marked.
- Local files can be dragged from Portside into other macOS applications as
  ordinary file drags. Portside offers copy only to an external destination,
  so completing that drag never removes the original.
- The global header now carries the design's Favorites, Connect, Search, and
  Appearance controls. Names get more room by default, and each pane remembers
  its resized file-table columns across tabs and relaunches.

### Known limitations

- SFTP cannot prove mount or stable directory identity with protocol v3, so
  copying a folder from SFTP, cross-provider folder merging, overwriting a
  folder on either side of an SFTP operation, and permanently deleting an SFTP
  folder are refused before mutation. Individual remote files and symbolic
  links can be deleted permanently; SFTP has no Trash.
- Deep search is local-only. SFTP source folders cannot be downloaded as whole
  trees, and separate SFTP connections cannot transfer directly between each
  other. Connection sharing between remote tabs is deferred, so a new tab from
  an SFTP tab starts at local Home.
- Each Mount Network Drive address must name exactly one SMB share root such as
  `smb://server/share`, not a folder inside it. Portside keeps no SMB connection
  history or password and does not auto-remount; macOS owns the authentication
  prompt and Keychain choice.
